summary.intent: Debug and fix two related bugs in CipherBox's macOS FUSE filesystem: (1) folder rename requiring elevated permissions and failing, and (2) web UI rename + manual sync creating a duplicate folder instead of renaming the existing one.
summary.outcome: Both bugs were diagnosed and fixed in the Rust FUSE crate, with 2 new unit tests and full e2e desktop test coverage added across bash/PowerShell FUSE operation tests and cross-client sync tests. All changes committed to branch fix/fuse-folder-rename.

repo: Project uses a custom gsd-debugger subagent (via gsd-tools.cjs) for debugging — this is the correct agent type, not general-purpose
Active debug sessions are tracked in .planning/debug/*.md files; session state is persisted across agent spawns
E2e desktop tests live in tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/ with both bash (.sh) and PowerShell (.ps1) variants that must be kept in sync
SDK utility scripts for simulating web UI actions live in packages/sdk-core/scripts/*.mjs
Encryption is the real access control in CipherBox — Unix permissions on FUSE inodes are not meaningful and should be permissive (0o777/0o666)

code.finding: populate_folder() matched children by display name only; when a folder is renamed remotely (same ipns_name, new name), find_child() returned None, a new inode was allocated, and the old inode was preserved via merge_only=true logic — creating duplicates. Fix: build ipns_name->ino lookup map and fall back to stable IPNS identifier when name-based match fails.

Directory permissions were 0o755 and file permissions 0o644. On macOS with FUSE-T's SMB backend, the SMB server performs its own permission check against getattr results — when SMB client UID doesn't match FUSE-reported owner, write ops (including rename) are denied, triggering Touch ID and ultimately failing. Fix: use 0o777/0o666.
New script: authenticates, loads vault metadata, calls renameInFolder(), republishes folder metadata — mirrors exactly what the web UI does when renaming a folder, enabling e2e sync tests.

workflow: When the /debug skill is invoked for an app-level bug (not a Claude Code bug), it activates session-level logging which is irrelevant — recognize this and redirect to application debugging immediately
The gsd-debugger subagent pattern burns context fast (reading files, forming hypotheses) — spawning fresh 200k context agents per investigation keeps the main context lean
FUSE-T SMB backend permission behavior on macOS cannot be unit tested — only manual verification on a mounted filesystem is possible for that class of fix
For cross-platform FUSE tests, bash and PowerShell test scripts must be updated in parallel to stay in sync

friction: First response spawned generic research agents instead of the project's custom gsd-debugger subagent — user had to interrupt and re-invoke with the correct agent type and context
The /debug skill was invoked first (activating Claude Code session logging) before recognizing this was an application-level bug, not a Claude Code issue — wasted a turn
open_items: Bug 1 (permission fix 0o755→0o777) has no automated test coverage — macOS FUSE-T SMB runtime behavior cannot be unit tested and requires manual verification on the mounted filesystem
Linux and Windows rename behavior has not been tested — unknown whether the same permission or sync bugs manifest on other platforms
Manual post-deploy verification needed: mount filesystem, confirm rename works without Touch ID dialog, confirm web UI rename + sync shows only renamed folder with no duplicate
